name: Varicocele
one_line: Varicocele is common, and many men who have one father children without treatment. Here is what it is and when doctors suggest fixing it.
who_this_is_for: For men told they have a varicocele, often found during a fertility check, and for their partners who want to understand what it means.
red_flags: Sudden, severe pain or swelling in a testicle: go to hospital now.
doctor_questions: Can you feel the varicocele on examination, or was it seen only on the scan?
What grade is it, and is it on one side or both?
Is it likely to be affecting my semen report?
Would repair help in our case, and what are the options?
How long after repair would we see any change in the semen report?
Should my partner have any tests while we decide?

faq.a: It is a swelling of the veins in the scrotum, a bit like varicose veins in the leg. It is most often on the left side. Many men have one and never know.

faq.q: Does a varicocele always cause infertility?
faq.a: No. Many men with a varicocele have normal semen and father children. It matters more when it can be felt on examination and the semen report is also abnormal.

Repair is usually considered when the varicocele can be felt, the semen report is abnormal, and the couple is having trouble conceiving. A small varicocele seen only on a scan is not usually treated for fertility. Your doctor decides with you.

The common options are microsurgery to tie off the affected veins, or embolisation, where the veins are blocked from inside by a radiologist. Both are usually done as day or short stay procedures. Any change in the semen report takes a few months to show.
